paragraphs: Rav Yaakov bar Abba (II). A student of Abaye and Rava.

In [Bava Metzia 23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.23b.6), where he found a jar of wine, he came before Abaye; and in [Eruvin 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.62b.12) he raised a difficulty against Abaye.

Likewise he raised an objection to Rava in [Eruvin 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.12b.7); he sat before Rava, as in [Zevachim 70b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.70b.3); and he happened to come to Rava's house and he called Rava “Master”, as in [Pesachim 103a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.103a.9).

And in [Kiddushin 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.31b.4) we find Rav Yaakov bar Abbahu asking Abaye: "For example, I, when I return from the study hall, my father holds up the cup for me and my mother mixes it for me, what should I do?" He said to him: "Accept from your mother, but from your father do not accept, since he is a Torah scholar and this may hurt his feelings." And Hyman argues that it appears he is Rav Yaakov bar Abba.

And in [Menachot 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.17a.8): Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi in the name of Abaye; and Hyman says one must emend, following the reading of Dikdukei Soferim [דק״ס], to “Rav Yaakov bar Abba said in Abaye’s name,” since Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi was a sage of the Land of Israel (a Yerushalmi amora), a student of Rabbi Yochanan.[^2]

notes.text: Pesachim 103a directly shows Yaakov addressing Rava as Master. Hyman’s proposed Abbahu/Abba identification and Idi-to-Abba emendation remain attributed; the exact Dikdukei Soferim reading was not independently inspected.
Kiddushin gives Yaakov bar Avuha, who asks Abaye about accepting service from his parents. Menachot gives Yaakov bar Idi transmitting in Abaye’s name. Hyman’s proposed bar Abba readings remain his.
